summary: The Love Lives On Act of 2025 amends titles 10 and 38 to let remarried surviving spouses keep receiving DIC payments under sections 1311/1562, SBP annuities for survivors of active-duty deaths (with retroactive resumption), and TRICARE coverage even after a later marriage ends.

scores.thoughts: The bill expands eligibility for Dependency and Indemnity Compensation, Survivor Benefit Plan annuities, and TRICARE coverage for remarried surviving spouses of veterans and service members. These changes directly increase federal outlays on mandatory benefits programs, constituting an expansion of government spending.
The bill contains no provisions altering tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.

Section 4 expands TRICARE eligibility to include remarried widows/widowers whose subsequent marriage has ended. TRICARE is a government-provided military health program, so the change modestly broadens public coverage rather than promoting private/market-based alternatives.
No provisions address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration, visas, border policy, or noncitizen benefits.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.

While the bill concerns survivors of military members and veterans, it adjusts post-service benefits rather than funding for defense procurement, operations, or force structure. It has no direct bearing on military or defense spending levels.
No environmental, energy, or regulatory provisions appear in the bill.

The legislation broadens access to veterans' survivor benefits (DIC, SBP, TRICARE), which function as targeted income and health supports for a specific population. This constitutes a modest expansion of the social safety net.
No education funding, school choice, or federal education policy provisions are present.
No drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance-related provisions exist.
No criminal sentencing, policing, or justice reform measures are included.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or import/export regulations are addressed.
By increasing mandatory federal spending without corresponding revenue or cuts, the bill implicitly accepts additional deficit spending rather than prioritizing debt reduction.
No provisions expand or restrict legal protections based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
No foreign assistance or international aid provisions are present.
No voting access, election administration, or campaign finance measures appear.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions exist.
No labor, union, or workplace rights provisions are included.
No religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination measures are addressed.
